# Erdős #30: Finite Sidon sets and smoothing

[All problems](../README.md) · [Lab](../../README.md) · [Progress](../../PROGRESS.md) · [Contribute](../../CONTRIBUTING.md)

**Project focus: RETAINED.** How large can a set of integers be when its nonzero differences never repeat?

## The question

For F(N), the largest size of a Sidon subset of {1,...,N} with unordered sums including repetitions, is F(N)=sqrt(N)+O_epsilon(N^epsilon) for every epsilon>0? Here a restricted theorem compares three-bin smoothing certificates, not F(N) itself.

## Read this first

The local scalar-versus-vector comparison is an analytical proof within the established Hou-Zhao method. It is weaker than published second-order constants, is not a global Sidon bound improvement, has unchecked literature priority and is not formalized in Lean.

## Next bounded question

For two symmetric three-bin kernels, can a sharp continuous lower bound be proved when the mixing weight is free, rather than fixed at 1/2?

**Discriminating test:** A feasible freely weighted two-kernel system below a proposed lower bound refutes that bound; a finite grid optimum cannot establish the continuous result.
